questions.question: Which of the following companies was conferred with Maharatna status in October 2019?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Limited was conferred with** Maharatna status in October 2019.**
 
• Two separate orders to this effect were issued by the** Department of Public Enterprises, under the Ministry of Heavy Industry and Public Enterprises**.
 
• The grant of Maharatna status to the PSUs will impart **enhanced powers to their Boards to take financial decisions.**
 
• The Boards of Maharatna **central public sector enterprises (CPSEs) can make equity investments to undertake financial joint ventures and wholly-owned subsidiaries and undertake mergers and acquisitions in India and abroad, **subject to a ceiling of 15 percent of the net worth of the concerned CPSE, limited to Rs 5,000 crore in one project.
 
• Boards can also structure and implement schemes relating to** personnel and human resource management and training. **
 
• They can also enter into technology joint ventures or other strategic alliances, among others.
 
• The holding companies of a **'Maharatna' PSU **are also empowered to transfer assets, float fresh equity and divest shareholding in subsidiaries, subject to the condition that the delegation will only be in respect of the subsidiaries set up by the holding company.
 
• **HPCL was incorporated in 1974** after the takeover and merger of erstwhile Esso Standard and Lube India through the Esso (Acquisition of Undertaking in India) Act passed by Parliament.
 
• **Power Grid Corporation of India Limited is India's largest electric power transmission utility firm. It is a listed company since 2007.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__** **List of Maharatna Companies in India 2022**

questions.question: Which Chola ruler was popularly called ‘Victor of the Ganges’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajendra Chola I.**__

__
 
• Rajendra Chola I was popularly called ‘Victor of the Ganges’.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• Rajendra I (1014 AD-1044 AD):
 
 
• He conquered Orissa, Bengal, Burma and Andaman and Nicobar islands.
 
• The** Chola dynasty was at its zenith **during his reign.
 
• Rajendra I also assumed the title of ‘***Gangaikonda Cholam***’ and built a city called **Gangaikonda Cholapuram.**
 
• Rajendra I conquered complete Sri Lanka and made** Anuradhapura **his capital.
 
• He defeated the **Pala king Mahipala** and took the title of **Gangaikonda Cholam.**
 
• He also built the **Cholamandalam Lake** and the city of Gangikonda Cholapuram.
 
• He won the Java, Sumatra and Malaya areas from the Shailendra king.
 
 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Chola Empire (850 AD-1279 AD):
 
 
• **Capital: Tanjore, Gangaikonda Cholapuram.**
 
• The **founder **of the Chola dynasty was ***Vijayalaya***, who was at first a feudatory of the Pallavas.
 
• He captured Tanjore in 850 AD.
 
• The **ancient capital of Cholas was Palyarai.**
 
• Vijayalaya revived the Chola Empire in the 9th century AD.
 
 
• He took the title of ‘***Narkesari***’.

questions.question: In which year did the JavaScript Programming language come into existence?

• JavaScript is a** programming language** used in web development.
 
• It was **developed by Netscape **to add dynamic and interactive elements to websites. 
 
• JavaScript is** influenced by Java.**
 
• It is a** client-side scripting language.**
 
• A JavaScript code can be inserted anywhere within the HTML of a webpage.

• It was originally named Mocha, but quickly became known as **LiveScript and, later, JavaScript.**

questions.question: India shares its land boundaries with which countries in the east?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Myanmar and Bangladesh.**__

__
 
• India shares a **1,643-km-long** border with **Myanmar **which touches the states of **Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur and Mizoram.**
 
• India shares a **4,096-km-long** border with **Bangladesh **which touches **Assam, Tripura, Mizoram, Meghalaya and West Bengal.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The border with **Bangladesh **is guarded by the **Border Security Force(BSF)**.
 
• The border with **Myanmar **is guarded by **Assam Rifles(AR).**
 
• The **Indo-China **border is guarded by **Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP).**
 
• The** Indo-Pakistan** is guarded by **Border Border Security Force (BSF).**
 
• The** Indo-Nepal** is guarded by Border **Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB).**
 
• The** Indo-Bhutan** is guarded by Border **Sashastra Seema Bal (SSB).**

questions.question: How many agro-climatic zones (ACZ) are characterized by the Planning Commission of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**15.**__

__
 
• 15 agro-climatic zones (ACZ) are characterized by the Planning Commission of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• An Agro-climatic zone is a** land unit in form of major climates **that are suitable for a certain range of crops and cultivators. 
 
• **National Agricultural Research Project (NARP) was launched by ICAR** for initiating agricultural research in the agro-climatic zones of the country.
 
 
• The purpose was to set up and upgrade a zonal research station in each agro-climatic zone for creating location-specific, need-based research targeted for specific agro-ecological situations.
 
• In NARP, the country is divided into **127 agro-climatic zones.**
 
 
 
• The agro-climatic zone division helps to achieve optimum utilization in a suitable manner within the framework of resource constraints and potentials of each region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Planning Commission of India:
 
 
• The Planning Commission formulated India's Five-Year Plans.
 
• It was formed in** March 1950.**
 
• It was **replaced by NITI Aayog **in the year **2015.**
 
 
 
• NITI Aayog:
 
 
• ​NITI Aayog or National Institution for Transforming India Aayog is the replacement of Planning Commission of India.

questions.question: What is the mission life of the Cartosat-3 satellite launched by PSLV C-47 on 27 November 2019?

• **Hyperspectral-Capture**s light from the electromagnetic spectrum
 
• **Multispectral-Captures** light within specific ranges of the electromagnetic spectrum.
 
 
 
• The** Indian Space Research Organization** launched **13 commercial nanosatellites** of the **United States **along with the imaging and mapping satellite Cartostat-3.
 
• PSLV-C47 is a **Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle** into Sun Synchronous Orbit from Satish Dhawan Space Centre at Sriharikota.

questions.question: ‘Sattriya’ is a traditional Hindu classical dance form of which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Assam.**__

__
 
• **‘Sattriya’ is a traditional Hindu classical dance form of Assam.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sattriya—Assam:**

 
 
• The Sattriya dance of Assam is a classical form of dance, which is highly devotional in character with the spiritual aspect being predominant.
 
• **The word ‘Sattriya’ is derived from ‘Sattra’which means ‘monastery’.**
 
• The dance developed and grew within the Satras, it is named after these religious institutions.
 
• It emerges from a 5**00–year-old comprehensive theatre tradition** nurtured in the **Vaishnav Monasteries of Assam.**
 
• There were two dance forms prevalent in Assam before the **neo-Vaishnava movement**, such as ***Ojapali ***and ***Devadasi ***with many classical elements.
 
• As far as Devadasi dance is concerned, the resemblance of a good number of rhythmic syllables and dance postures along with footwork with Sattriya dance is a clear indication of the influence of the former on the latter.
 
• Sattriya dance tradition is governed by strictly laid-down principles in respect of **hasta mudras, footwork, acharyas, music,** etc.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ghumura, Chau, Goti Pua, Nacni, Odissi** are traditional classical dance form of **Odisha**.
 
• **Thang-Ta, Dhol Cholom** are traditional classical dance form of **Manipur**.
 
• **Dekhnni, Fugdi, Corridinho, Dashavatara **are traditional classical dance form of **Goa**.

questions.question: Which of the following is a famous fossil site in India where a full-fledged skeleton of a dinosaur was found?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Waddham, Maharashtra.**__

__
 
• Wadham, Maharashtra is a famous fossil site in India where a full-fledged skeleton of a dinosaur was found.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Waddham** is a reserve forest and is a well-known fossils site where a full-fledged skeleton of a dinosaur was found near the Godavari Basin in 1959.
 
• Paleolithic(stone age) tools were discovered in Wadham, Maharashtra.
 
• The well preserved **Barapasaurus skeleton** found at the site is at present kept in the **museum of Indian Statistical Institute (ISI) in Kolkata.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Manendragarh, Chhattisgarh is well known for a **sanctuary of marine fossils.**

 
 
• The Marine Gondwana Fossil Park is a unique appearance of **fossiliferous marine Permian rocks **of the Talchir formation recording back to around 280-240 million years ago. 
 
 
 
• Zanskar Valley of Kashmir is known for the world’s most diverse marine animals.
 
 
• The **trilobites at the Kurgiakh region of the Zanskar Valley** are from the beginning of the Cambrian age and are similar to those found in South China and parts of Pakistan.
 
 
 
• Hathnora of Madhya Pradesh is well known for** India’s earliest human fossils.**

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of the most explosive type of volcano?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Calderas volcanoes.**__

__
 
• Calderas volcanoes are an example of the most explosive type of volcano.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• Caldera Volcanoes:
 
 
• Calderas Volcanoes are known as the most explosive volcanoes on Earth.
 
• When they erupt, they incline to drop on themselves rather than constructing any structure.
 
• The fallen depressions are known as **calderas.**
 
 

**​** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/945720746a7541072be9595eb918322b43399177ccf570c34121e52b5d0dc24d.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Volcanoes:
 
 
• A volcano is a vent or fissure in Earth’s crust through which lava, ash, rocks, and gases erupt.
 
 
 
• The other types of volcanoes are** **Shield Volcanoes and Composite Volcanoes. 
 
• Shield volcanoes:
 
 
• These are the** largest of all the volcanoes on the earth.**
 
• These volcanoes are **made up of basalt.**
 
• Eg: Hawaiian shield volcanoes.
 
 
 
• Flood Basalt volcanoes:
 
 
• These volcanoes **discharge highly fluid lava **that flows for** long distances.**
 
• Most parts of the world are covered by thick basalt lava flows.

questions.question: How many parathyroid glands are present on the back side of the thyroid gland in humans?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Four.**__

__
 
• Four parathyroid glands are present on the backside of the thyroid gland in humans​.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Parathyroid Gland:**

 
 
• The glands are small **pea-sized glands **located in the neck just behind the butterfly-shaped thyroid gland.
 
• Everyone has **four parathyroid glands**, with two parathyroid glands lying behind each 'wing' of the thyroid gland.
 
• **Parathyroid hormone**: This hormone is secreted when there is a** deficiency of calcium in the blood.**
 
• **Calcitonin**: This hormone is released when there is an excess of calcium in the blood.
 
 
• A hormone secreted by the parathyroid gland controls the quantity of calcium in the blood. 
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Exocrine glands**: Glands which **have duct **are called exocrine glands. Secretion of enzymes passes through it.

 
 
• Example:** Lactic gland, Sweat gland.**
 
 
 
• **Endocrine glands**: These are **ductless glands.** Hormones are secreted by these glands.
 
 
• Hormones are sent to the different parts of the body through blood plasma.
 
• Example: **Pituitary gland, Thyroid gland.**

questions.question: In 1930, which scientist was awarded the Nobel Prize for describing the human ABO blood group system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Karl Landsteiner.**__

__
 
• In 1930, Karl Landsteiner was awarded the Nobel Prize for describing the human ABO blood group system

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Karl Landsteiner **discovered human blood groups in the year **1900.**
 
• The discovery laid the foundation for the modern medical practice of blood transfusion.
 
• Karl Landsteiner**​**__ himself considered it an accidental discovery.
 
• On the basis of the presence of **Antigen or Glycoprotein, **there are four groups of blood in human:
 __
 
• That contains Antigen A–Blood **Group A.**
 
• That contains Antigen B–Blood **Group B.**
 
• That contains **both the Antigens A and B**–Blood **Group AB.**
 
• That contains **neither of the Antigens**– Blood **Group O.**
 
 
 
• Blood **Group O** is called the **Universal Donor.**
 
• Blood **Group AB** is called** Universal Receptor.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **The Nobel Prize in Medicine 1974** was awarded jointly to **Albert Claude, Christian de Duve and George E. Palade** "for their discoveries concerning the **structural and functional organization of the cell."**
 
• George Wald with Haldan K. Hartline and Ragnar Granit of Sweden received the** Nobel Prize for Physiology or Medicine in 1967** for his work on the **chemistry of vision.**
 
• **Roger Guillemin and Andrew Schally** shared the Nobel Prize in** Medicine and Physiology in 1977** for their work on neurohormones.

questions.question: How many elements of India were listed in the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity as of March 2018?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**13.**__

__
 
• 13 elements of India were listed in the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity as of March 2018.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• National List of Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH) of India:
 
 
• **Ministry of Culture** launched the National List of Intangible Cultural Heritage (ICH) of India. 
 
• The National ICH List is an effort to recognize the diversity of Indian culture rooted in its intangible heritage.
 
• The initiative is also a part of the **Vision 2024 of the Ministry of Culture.**
 
 
 
• **UNESCO’s List of Intangible Cultural Heritage****:**
 
 
• **​**The list was established in 2008 when the Convention for Safeguarding of the Intangible Cultural Heritage came into effect. 
 
• UNESCO maintains **three lists under its “Intangible Cultural Heritage”**:
 
 
• The list of intangible cultural heritage in need of urgent safeguarding.
 
• The list of the intangible cultural heritage of humanity.
 
• The register of good safeguarding practices.

questions.question: When was the Backward and Minority Communities Employees Federation (BAMCEF) established in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1978.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• The Backward and Minority Communities Employees Federation (BAMCEF) established in the year **1978.**
 
• ‘**BAMCEF**’ is working since **1973 **and is known to **Mulnivasi Bahujan Samaj** as an organization of the educated employees from the Scheduled castes, Scheduled tribes, Other Backward Classes and the Converted Minority communities. 
 
• The term Backward has been mentioned in **article 16(4) of the Constitution of India.**
 
• The** S.C., ST. and O.B.C.** have been jointly referred to as Backwards because all the castes, falling in these categories, are backward.
